gumtree_entries.description: DELETED o2: Undeclared exception!
DELETED o5: Undeclared exception!
DELETED o7: Undeclared exception!
ADDED i2: Builder configured with a 5-byte array yields a stream whose available() reports the full array length.
ADDED i3: Skipping zero bytes consumes nothing: it returns 0 and leaves all bytes available.
ADDED i4: Skipping a negative number of bytes is rejected with IllegalArgumentException.
ADDED i6: When the offset is clamped to the (small) array length there is nothing left to read, so a subsequent skip returns 0 and available() is 0.
ADDED i7: Reading into a destination buffer reads as many bytes as the buffer holds (1) and decrements the remaining available count accordingly.
ADDED i8: With an offset beyond the array, the stream is already at end-of-data: available() is 0 and read(byte[]) returns -1 (end of stream).
ADDED i9: Reading with a requested length of 0 returns 0 without consuming any bytes.
ADDED i10: A single-byte readable window (offset 1, length 1 over a 3-byte array) returns that byte's value (0) and leaves nothing available.
ADDED i11: With offset 1 on a 1-byte array the stream starts already exhausted, so read() returns -1 (end of stream).
ADDED i12: A window of offset 1 / length 1 over a 2-byte array leaves exactly one byte available.
ADDED i13: Constructing with a negative offset is rejected with IllegalArgumentException.
ADDED i15: An empty array with an offset produces a stream with nothing available.
ADDED i16: Builder.setOffset rejects a negative offset with IllegalArgumentException.
ADDED i18: Builder.setOffset returns the same builder instance to support fluent chaining.
ADDED i19: Builder.setLength rejects a negative length with IllegalArgumentException.
ADDED i21: Builder.setLength returns the same builder instance to support fluent chaining.
ADDED i22: Calling reset() before any read keeps all bytes available (resets to the initial mark).
ADDED i23: Reading into a buffer the size of the stream consumes everything: it returns the full count and leaves nothing available.
ADDED i24: markSupported() is always true and does not consume any bytes.
ADDED i25: With an offset beyond the array, available() is 0 even before any read.
ADDED i26: mark() with a (negative) read limit is accepted and does not change availability.
